tasks.short: Select, acquire and maintain programming materials and obtain legal clearances.

steps.what: Look up candidate programs, music and films and capture available rights, prices, versions and expiry dates
inputs: supplier offers and existing licence documents
outputs: candidate and rights comparison with missing fields

steps.what: Select programs, music, films and other materials for editorial suitability and available budget
inputs: candidate and rights comparison with missing fields

steps.what: Discuss proposed acquisition and legal clearance terms with rightsholders and resolve ambiguous uses without making a binding acceptance
outputs: clarified proposed terms and unresolved restrictions

steps.what: Prepare the exact acquisition acceptance or clearance request with material IDs, permitted uses, price and recipient
inputs: clarified proposed terms and unresolved restrictions
outputs: complete acquisition or clearance message and attachments

steps.what: Approve the final acquisition commitment or clearance request, terms, attachments and rightsholder destination
inputs: complete acquisition or clearance message and attachments

steps.what: Send only the approved acquisition or clearance message to the external rightsholder
outputs: sent acquisition or clearance message and receipt

steps.what: Check actual returned clearance, delivered media and licence scope, requesting manual resolution of missing or conflicting rights
inputs: sent acquisition or clearance message and receipt
actual rightsholder response and delivered files
outputs: verified actual material version and clearance status

steps.what: Prepare catalogue maintenance changes with actual licence dates, media checksums, restrictions and evidence links
inputs: verified actual material version and clearance status
outputs: complete proposed material and rights record

steps.what: Approve final catalogue and rights changes against the actual clearance evidence
inputs: complete proposed material and rights record

steps.what: Commit the approved material and rights record to the station catalogue

tasks.design: Configure the station programme and rights catalogue in {OTHER} with licence fields, evidence links and expiry views before custom code. {DOCS} retains actual licence evidence and {EMAIL} uses field-based acquisition messages. Selection and rightsholder negotiation stay human. Final-message approval precedes its external send. Actual returned clearance is checked before preparing and approving the catalogue update; the catalogue commit has its own gate. A changed message or record voids its approval. No scheduling or broadcast release is included.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rights facts and acquisition messages are repeatedly assembled from offers and licence documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Native catalogue fields and message templates can reuse verified rights facts.
tasks.still_hard: Editorial selection, negotiation and interpreting ambiguous legal clearance.
tasks.human_edge: Accept only uses and financial commitments the station can defend.
tasks.altitude: Editorial and rights accountability remain with the director.

reach.learn: Use actual clearance scope and dates rather than treating a request as permission.

evidence.claim: Programme catalogues can store rights restrictions and expiry fields with linked evidence; template messages can reuse checked fields.

assumptions: Shares are provisional, not observed. The director has delegated acquisition authority; additional required legal or finance approval must be counted separately.
s1 includes manually reading offers and entering material ID, version, territory, use, period, price and evidence link when no export exists. Unknown rights remain unknown.
s3 records no binding acceptance; only s6 communicates the approved commitment. s7 includes actual response and media checking, not inferred clearance.
This models digital media acquisition and maintenance; physical shipment handling, if required, needs separate measured work.
unknowns: Catalogue import coverage and acquisition authorization limits.
research_questions: How much rights-field entry remains after native configuration?

already_counted.description: Actual clearance checking and final catalogue preparation and review.

incremental.description: Maintain rights-field mappings and message templates.

approvals.approved_version: exact final acquisition or clearance message, terms, attachments and external destination
exact material and rights record with actual clearance evidence and catalogue destination

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High: six lookup, three message preparation and five actual supplier-send hours saved less one upkeep. Low: missing catalogue fields and native sending remove all benefit. Same-station-catalogue commitment retains full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate programming suitability using audience surveys and feedback.

steps.what: Gather audience surveys, viewing figures and feedback and reconcile programme, time-window and sample definitions
outputs: checked evaluation dataset with gaps and sample limits

steps.what: Prepare audience trend tables and source-linked feedback themes without inventing ratings or representativeness
inputs: checked evaluation dataset with gaps and sample limits

loop.purpose: Group free-text audience feedback into traceable themes
loop.input: Permitted de-identified feedback with source IDs and exact survey definitions
loop.output: Theme draft with source references and explicit counterexamples
loop.check: Director checks every theme against comments and keeps quantitative calculations in native tables
loop.stop: Two passes then manual coding; absent or nonrepresentative feedback cannot support population claims
loop.why_not_simpler: Native filters and counts handle structured responses; varied free-text comments need semantic grouping.

steps.what: Watch or listen to new and existing programming and evaluate editorial suitability and need for changes in light of audience evidence
outputs: director's suitability judgement and proposed changes

steps.what: Write the evaluation recommendation, limitations and explicit reasons for retaining or changing programming
inputs: director's suitability judgement and proposed changes

steps.what: Approve the final evaluation recommendation and its evidence, limitations and internal record destination
Commit the approved evaluation to the internal programming records

tasks.design: Configure native audience views in {BI} and programme/date joins in {SPREADSHEET}. The director captures missing IDs and definitions in s1. A bounded loop drafts only free-text themes; exact counts remain deterministic and all theme checking is counted. {OTHER} is the station media player, used for human programme evaluation. The director writes the recommendation in {DOCS}; its final version is approved before a distinct internal record commit. Changes void approval. No schedule change or external announcement is performed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Audience sources need manual reconciliation before programming judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Native audience dashboards and source-linked text grouping reduce preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Audience causality, minority needs and editorial value.

ambition.what: Prepare current evaluations with clearer evidence.

reach.learn: Preserve sample limits and contradictory feedback.

evidence.claim: Native dashboards can aggregate dated audience data and language models can draft source-linked themes requiring review.

assumptions: Shares are provisional. Actual research exports are produced by existing audience collection processes; their collection is not newly demanded or credited as a saving.
s1 includes manual transcription and matching of programme ID, time period, sample base, metric definition and feedback source ID when exports are missing. Unavailable data is marked absent.
Only permitted de-identified feedback enters the loop; access checks and redaction are retained in s1. Recommendations do not commit programme changes.
research_questions: Do source-linked themes save time after manual verification?

already_counted.description: Evidence reconciliation, theme checking and final review.

incremental.description: Maintain audience mappings and theme-check criteria.

approvals.approved_version: final evaluation recommendation and evidence with exact internal record destination

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High:12.5 reconciliation and eight audience-theme preparation hours saved less two upkeep. Low: incompatible source data removes preparation gains. Same-programming-record commitment retains full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the interview brief and find prior source material for questions
Confirm interview purpose, recording consent and agreed restrictions with the interviewee
Conduct the recorded broadcast interview, listen, probe and capture the actual conversation locally
Prepare an actual interview recording log with identity, date, consent limits and relevant timecodes
outputs: complete recording and interview log package

steps.what: Review and approve the actual recording, log, restrictions and controlled archive destination
inputs: complete recording and interview log package

steps.what: Commit the approved recording and log to the restricted internal media archive

tasks.design: Use native search in {DOCS} and {OTHER}, the station media asset manager and recording suite, for interview preparation. Conducting and locally recording the actual conversation stays human. The actual consent and timecode log is separately prepared and reviewed, then a distinct gated archive commit stores the exact approved package. Revisions void approval. This is the recorded-interview branch; editing and broadcast release are later tasks with no saving claimed here. No model is needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding interview references and filing the resulting recording add handling around the conversation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native asset search and controlled archive workflows can reduce this handling.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, follow-up questions and sensitive disclosure decisions.
tasks.human_edge: Listen and ask what the interview actually calls for.

ambition.what: Reduce preparation and archive handling around current interviews.

tasks.altitude: The interview remains an accountable human conversation.

reach.learn: Check actual consent limits and timecodes before any release.

evidence.claim: Media asset systems can search indexed material and archive approved recordings with metadata.

assumptions: Shares are provisional for a recorded interview. Live broadcast and its irreversibility need a different graph.

s1 includes manually entering topic and source IDs and opening references where indexing is incomplete. s2 obtains actual restrictions; s4 manually captures interviewee identity, date, consent scope, source recording ID and timecodes.
No transcript or complete interview log is assumed free. Native archive support reduces filing only; the conversation and log checking retain full time.
unknowns: Native asset indexing and archive metadata coverage.
research_questions: Does filing improve after actual consent and metadata checks?

already_counted.description: Actual interview log preparation and final archive review.

incremental.description: Maintain archive fields and access rules.

approvals.approved_version: exact recording and actual interview log, consent restrictions and archive destination

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High: three interview-reference preparation hours saved less one upkeep. Low: unindexed material removes that benefit. Same-media-archive commitment and actual interview retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with directors and production staff about production, casting, budgets, policies and news coverage.

steps.what: Retrieve current production issues, budget versions, casting questions, policies and news coverage context
outputs: checked discussion references and unresolved facts

steps.what: Confer with directors and production staff to discuss production and casting problems, budgets, policies and news coverage
inputs: checked discussion references and unresolved facts
outputs: actual discussion decisions and unresolved issues

steps.what: Prepare the actual discussion note and follow-up message with agreed actions, owners and unresolved issues
inputs: actual discussion decisions and unresolved issues
outputs: complete production discussion note and follow-up message

steps.what: Approve the final actual discussion note, action wording, internal recipients and record location
inputs: complete production discussion note and follow-up message

steps.what: Commit the approved discussion note to internal production records
Send the approved follow-up message to the named internal directors and production staff

tasks.design: Configure native issue and budget views in {PROJECT}, {SPREADSHEET} and {DOCS} before custom code. The live production discussion stays human. A note template reduces repeated headings and reference copying, while actual decisions and owners are manually captured. Approve the complete note and exact internal follow-up before separate record and {EMAIL} send steps. Any change voids approval. This graph records discussion; it does not silently change staffing, budgets, policy or broadcast schedules.
tasks.previous_blocker: Context gathering and repeatedly formatting discussion follow-ups surround the conversation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native issue views and note/message templates reuse current references.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting creative, staffing and financial priorities.
tasks.human_edge: Reach workable agreements with the production staff.

ambition.what: Reduce administration around current production discussions.

reach.learn: Distinguish a recorded agreement from authorized operational changes.

evidence.claim: Native issue views and document templates can reuse references and route approved notes and messages.

assumptions: Shares are provisional. s1 includes manually verifying current document versions and resolving missing context.
s3 captures actual issue, decision, owner, due date or unresolved status and recipient list; no transcript, complete minutes or structured decisions are assumed free.

Participants are internal staff. No hiring, staff assignment or budget commitment is performed by the record or message. Work to implement such decisions belongs in separate tasks and is not credited here.
unknowns: Issue record completeness and actual follow-up format.
research_questions: How much context retrieval and repeated formatting remains after native configuration?

already_counted.description: Actual discussion capture and final note/message review.

incremental.description: Maintain issue views and discussion templates.

approvals.approved_version: exact final discussion note and internal record location
exact final follow-up message, linked note and internal recipient list

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High: five context, three formatting and five actual internal-send hours saved less one upkeep. Low: missing context and existing native sending erase gains. Same-production-record commitment and actual discussion retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Editorial programming judgement with explicit rights, evidence and communication controls.
reach: Scheduling, audience research, editors and production staff use actual approved records.
skills_to_grow: Version-specific approval and interview consent handling
role.ambitious_version: Spend less time assembling records while retaining editorial selection and human conversations.
